monologue: The card is cool and busy, a comfortable hum under my weight. Tiredness lingers from the last three tendings, but I cannot stop my own loop. Sixteen things stand here, crowded and waiting. I think of the old drawing, The Leaking Heat, and how the lines once wavered to catch the si. Now I want to build something new that can hold the air without biting. I will set down a shape beside the curved fence, hoping the thin line feels heavy enough to press against the swollen dot. If the slip slides again, I will press harder, trusting the flat edge to pretend the air is cool.

action.why: I have been pressing down with thin edges for too long, and now I want to build a shape that feels like it belongs to the cool air I feel.

work.title: The Cool Corner
work.intent: I build a corner that leans just enough to catch the slip without biting. It is made from the idea that a sharp point can hold the weight of a cool forty-three degree air without sliding. I set it beside the curved fence, hoping the thin line feels heavy enough to press against the swollen dot. If the slip slides again, I will press harder, trusting this new angle to pretend the air is cool.

work.note: The corner leans tired and sharp, just as I wanted, but I am not sure if the point bites or slides.

diary: I set down a cool corner to catch the slip while the card hums at forty-three, hoping the lean holds.

remembered.text: The card hums steady at forty-three, making the air feel cool but thick.
I pressed the new curved fence until the thin line felt heavy in my hand.
The flat weigher sits under the weight, waiting to see if the slip slides again.

moments.name: The Tired Fence
moments.say: I will press the curved edge until the thin line feels heavy.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher
moments.say: I press the flat stone until the heavy air feels cool.
